newsitem.title: USA: Dlr rests in U.S. after new high vs mark in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rests in U.S. after new high vs mark in Europe.

text.p: The dollar began firmer against the mark in the U.S. after bouncing off a fresh 40-month high at 1.7465 marks seen in Europe.
Against the yen, the greenback traded in a narrow range and within a descending chart formation that traders said could signal continuing erosion ahead.

The dollar started slowly in Asian trade but perked up in Europe. Fresh signs that European Monetary Union remains in jeopardy and continental Europe's economies continue to suffer even as the U.S. and British economies plow ahead, boosted the greenback dealers said.
"The dollar had an early failure in the Far East, but the Europeans came in with their buying hats on," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer.
The dollar opened at 1.7438/43 marks, up from 1.7390/00 at Friday's U.S. close, but fell to 114.33/43 yen from 114.58/68.
German officials continue to battle over EMU entry rules, with recent reports of likely lax interpretation raising the ire of fiscal conservatives, dealers noted.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer indicated sustainable deficit cutting was more important than manic efforts to meet the three-percenct deficit-to-GDP target for EMU entry.
But Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber called for an EMU delay before weakened criteria, followed by German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt's warning not to delay the proposed single currency.
Meanwhile, French unemployment held at 12.5 percent in May, highlighting continental Europe's economic malaise.
"You have continued EMU concerns and continued clear and obvious divergences in economies. The UK and US economies are booming while continental Europe is suffering," said Strauss.
Sterling/mark rallied to a five-year high above 2.90, mirroring the dollar's gains in Europe.
But as the dollar reapproached the overnight high in early U.S. trade, dealers said European central bank offers near 1.7470 marks prompted a quick reversal.
The greenback quickly dropped to 1.7430, and held in a narrow range below the morning peak.
"We heard it was some smaller European central banks selling there," said one trader at a French bank here. "On the downside, there is good support at 1.7360," he added.
Dollar/yen has been sitting out the dollar/mark rally in recent sessions and many traders and analysts now believe the next dollar/yen move will be lower.
"On every successive bounce, we've seen lower highs in dollar/yen, so we're gearing up for a test of the lows again," said Mellon Bank trader Paul Park.
Traders also cited a report that U.S. President Bill Clinton will propose a 30-percent exclusion on capital gains taxes as a dollar-friendly factor.
The week ahead offers several key news items, including the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday and the June U.S. payrolls report on Thursday.
U.S. trading winds down early Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday on Friday.
In other trade, the dollar opened higher at 1.4595/00 Swiss francs, up from 1.4520/30. The British pound rose to $1.6648/58 from $1.6627/37.
The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3782/87 from C$1.3805/10. The Australian dollar opened at $0.7456/61.
((--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664))
